content:
Hi Veil team! A couple of us at Logical Intelligence have been messing around with Veil a bit, and we wrote a tactic #synthesize_invariants which, given a Veil module and its safety property will either return a set of inductive invariants, a counterexample to the safety property, state that no universal invariant exists, or time out with "unknown" (it is a semi-algorithm). Under the hood the tactic runs the universal PDR algorithm provided in this paper.

We were thinking it might be helpful to upstream it. We have tested it on several of the example files in the Veil repo, and it is able to successfully find invariants on all of them*. These include DecentralizedLock, RicartAgrawala, IvyTwoPhaseCommit, TlaTwoPhaseCommit, Ring, Peterson, RiverCrossing, DieHard, Traffic. It correctly found counterexamples for the latter three, and inductive invariants for the rest. This work is closely related to you guys' work in https://pirlea.net/papers/force-iclp25.pdf, I wonder if the two efforts can combine in some way eventually.

There are some limitations to our implementation:

  1. It is restricted to a fragment of Veil. It supports uninterpreted sorts, enums, bools, relations, functions, int/nat as values, and theories given as type class instances with axioms (eg TotalOrder)
  2. It only finds universal invariants (formulas starting with ∀\forall∀)
  3. The "no universal invariant" result is not proven sound, this is a followup as it requires some many-sorted model theory that mathlib does not have. The other two possible outcomes are indeed proven sound.

My branch on my personal fork is here, if you guys are interested in having this I'm happy to split this into a few PRs. It's about 4k lines of Lean, not counting tests

*we only tested on modules which are in the restricted fragment mentioned in limitation 1

@Tanner Duve This is amazing!

We've been thinking about formalising invariant inference algorithms ever since we starting working on Veil, but other things always took priority.

Definitely do make PRs for this -- we'd really want to upstream it.
@Tanner Duve Thanks! Will try to review over the weekend. (@Qiyuan Zhao is preparing some big merges as well, but I think they mostly shouldn't interfere.)
